increment_paragraph: **RETURN-FAMILY-CONDITIONAL-CONSTANT-PRUNING** (USER DECISION 2026-11-24: "launch the conditional-access follow-up cards"; gateway rule 74z, amending rule 74x; `QCore.ReturnFamilyConditionalConstant`; [report](../../reports/return-family-conditional-constant-pruning/README.md)). Rule 74x made every untracked root of both arms of an accessed conditional a base and never decided the condition, so `long w(const struct s *q) { const struct s *p = 0; return (0 ? p : q)->n; }` was `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`), though C never evaluates `p` (C11 6.5.15p4). `arm_roots` now calls `conditional_arm_roots`, which classifies both arms as before. When `constant::constant_condition` decides the condition, it keeps only the evaluated arm's roots. The accepted grammar is integer literals (decimal, octal, hex, `u`/`l`/`ll` suffixes), parentheses, unary `+ - ! ~` and the binary integer operators, evaluated exactly under the LP64 premise (C11 literal types, the usual arithmetic conversions, modular unsigned arithmetic). Names (enumeration constants included), `sizeof`, casts, calls, floats, characters, division by zero, signed overflow and out-of-range or negative shifts are undecided and keep rule 74x's reading. Only rule 74x's bases are pruned. The old tests, the may-bind refusal and the unclassified-arm refusal still read the untaken arm, so the tip discharges nothing rule 74x kept except a base of an arm C never evaluates (`only_dropped_bases_are_discharged`, `pruning_removes_only_unevaluated_bases`). Rule 10z and the `if` routes already prune such constants, so the readers agree. Family S reads the preprocessed stream, so a macro that expands to a literal is decided as that literal; the report asks the user to confirm that reading. Pinned at unit level (`constVectors`, 41 rows; `pruneVectors`, 22 rows) and end to end (9 admitted rows, 10 undecided rows, 3 kept-obligation rows); the change pins fail with the decision disabled. Two rule 74x pins that spelled a constant condition are respelled with an undecided one. Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6: no row moves (1,171 / 2 / 3,623 / 8 at both), as predicted; the census finds no accessed conditional in a `return` on the route. The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run. Registered: RETURN-FAMILY-UNTAKEN-ARM-DIRECT-BASES.

ledger.why: Discharged by RETURN-FAMILY-CONDITIONAL-CONSTANT-PRUNING (rule 74z). In crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_return_family.rs, `arm_roots` calls the new `conditional_arm_roots`, which classifies both arms of a conditional as rule 74x did. When the new `legacy_return_family_constant.rs` decides the condition as an integer constant expression (literals with C11 suffixes, parentheses, unary `+ - ! ~`, the binary integer operators; exact under the LP64 premise with C11 literal typing and the usual arithmetic conversions), it pushes only the roots of the arm C evaluates (C11 6.5.15p4). Division or modulo by zero, signed overflow, out-of-range or negative shifts, names, `sizeof`, casts and every other form are undecided and keep both arms. The old tests and refusals are unchanged, so the only discharged obligations are bases of an arm C never evaluates (`QCore.ReturnFamilyConditionalConstant.only_dropped_bases_are_discharged`, `pruning_removes_only_unevaluated_bases`, `pruned_covers_every_run`, `undecided_keeps_74x_reading`, `signed_arith_exact`). `(0 ? p : q)->n`, `(1 ? q : p)->n` and `((2 - 2) ? p : q)->n`, with a null local `p` and a formal `q`, are pinned `Safe` end to end (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/return_family_untracked_conditional_access/constant_pruning.rs). The undecided conditions stay `Unknown`, and the change pins fail with the decision disabled. Rule 10z and the `if` routes already prune these constants. The opt-in corpus measurement shows no move, as predicted (report §6). The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run. A macro that expands to a literal is decided as its expansion (report §3; a user decision is requested).

ledger.title: Family S's old tests read the roots of a conditional's untaken arm under a constant condition
ledger.text: RETURN-FAMILY-CONDITIONAL-CONSTANT-PRUNING (rule 74z) prunes only rule 74x's bases of the arm C never evaluates. Family S's old tests (the direct tests and rules 74r's, 74t's and 74w's walks) still read every root of both arms. So `return 0 ? p->n : q->n;` and `return (0 ? p->next : q)->n;` with a null local `p` stay `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`), while rule 10z and the `if` routes prune the same constant (`if (0) return p->n;` is `Safe`). The declaration form `long v = (0 ? p : q)->n;` is `Unknown` too (report §2 probe). This is precision, not soundness. DISCHARGE: prune by token position at every conditional whose condition rule 74z decides, in the old tests and the may-bind refusal alike; prove that every dropped base lies in an unevaluated arm and that no refusal is lost.
